 This is a paid press release. Contact the press release distributor directly with any inquiries. Stout Launches Loan-Level, Total Return Commercial Real Estate Debt Index, CREDX™
 PR Newswire Tue, November 17, 2026 at 5:03 AM PST 3 min read New monthly commercial real estate debt index covers more than 200,000 independently priced loans representing approximately over $750 billion, enabling granular benchmarking for categories such as property type, geography, loan structure and lender category. 
 CHICAGO, Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Stout today announced the launch of the "Moody's-Stout Total Return CRE Debt Index (CREDX™)", a loan-level, independently priced total return index for the commercial real estate ("CRE") debt market. CREDX gives lenders and investors a precise way to measure the performance of their loan books against like-for-like debt in the market, by metro area, lender type and loan type. 
 Stout is a global investment bank and advisory firm, specializing in corporate finance, valuation, financial disputes, and investigations. (PRNewsFoto/Stout) At $5.1 trillion, the CRE debt market is larger than municipal bonds, yet despite the size, maturity, and institutional sophistication, the market has lacked a high-frequency, asset-level return benchmark. CREDX fills that gap, using a well-vetted third-party loan valuation process, real loan transaction data, and a large and diversified repository of private CRE loans. The CREDX suite of over 6,000 indexes and loan metric data covers more than 200,000 loans representing over $750 billion in unpaid principal balance held over 500 banks, insurance companies, agencies, and debt funds. Each loan is priced using regularly updated loan financials, loan origination and sales data, and a SOC 1-audited pricing model that lenders and regulators have used for more than 20 years for financial reporting, audit and regulatory purposes. 
 "CREDX gives investors an independent benchmark that has been missing since I was a lender decades ago," said William S. Mercer , Managing Director at Stout. "What was true then is still true today; lenders need an independent benchmark to measure performance, to understand what drove that performance and how that data can be applied to future strategies." 
 Published monthly with data dating back to 2006, CREDX combines income and price returns into a single total return measure, with sub-indexes by property type, geography, loan structure, and lender category. Custom benchmarking enables lenders and investors to compare CRE debt portfolio performance against the broader market and peers, identify strengths and weaknesses, and make more informed portfolio decisions. 
 " Commercial real estate debt is a significant investment for key financial institutions, including banks and insurance companies ," said Mark Zandi, Chief Economist of Moody's Analytics. " Getting greater visibility under the hood of that huge, fragmented market can help investors identify and assess relative performance of their portfolios ." 
 Story Continues Beyond portfolio benchmarking, CREDX supports a range of applications, including underwriting guidance that shows where a lender's rates and terms sit relative to the market before a loan closes; fundraising and reporting that gives hard market comparisons for limited partners and boards; and C-suite strategy on capital allocation, target spreads and geographic expansion. 
 Portfolio managers can dig even deeper into performance analytics by combining CREDX performance data with their internal expected-loss information. Comparing risk-adjusted returns of the benchmark with those of their own portfolios allows institutions to distinguish stronger performance driven by sound underwriting and strategy versus exposure to more risky or volatile investments. 
 Learn more about CREDX and how to benchmark your CRE loan portfolio against the market by contacting William S. Mercer at Stout.
